extracted.intended_audience: parties, counsel, presiding officers, and participants in FCC adjudicative hearing proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and evidentiary rules governing exceptions, review, interlocutory actions, appeals, discovery, depositions, confidentiality, and protective orders in FCC hearing proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission-ordered nonfinality and review (20-day order)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may on its own initiative provide, by order adopted not later than 20 days after the time for filing exceptions expires, that an initial decision shall not become final, and that it shall be further reviewed or considered by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is discretionary Commission action to withhold finality of an initial decision; must be ordered within 20 days after the exceptions filing period expires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission actions on review of initial decision
rubrics_metrics.description: When an initial decision is subject to review, the Commission may hear oral argument on the exceptions; require filing of briefs; reopen the record and/or remand the proceedings to take further testimony or evidence; remand to make further findings or conclusions; or issue a supplemental initial decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any one or more of these actions may be taken prior to or after oral argument or filing of exceptions/briefs; used to assist resolution of issues on review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for effectiveness of initial decision (50-day rule and stays)
rubrics_metrics.description: No initial decision shall become effective before 50 days after public release of the full text thereof is made unless otherwise ordered by the Commission. The timely filing of exceptions, Commission-initiated further review, or action under paragraph (c) stays effectiveness until Commission review is completed. If effective date falls within any further time allowed for filing exceptions, it is postponed automatically until 30 days after time for filing exceptions has expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets default minimum delay before an initial decision becomes effective and describes automatic stays/postponements tied to exceptions and Commission action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic finality and public notice when no exceptions filed
rubrics_metrics.description: If no exceptions are filed, and the Commission has not ordered review or taken action under paragraph (c), the initial decision shall become effective, an appropriate notation entered in the docket, and a 'Public Notice' shall be given by the Commission. §1.108 does not apply to such public notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes how and when initial decisions become final absent exceptions or Commission review, and the public notice requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to file exceptions when application denial proposed
rubrics_metrics.description: When any party fails to file exceptions within the specified time to an initial decision which proposes to deny its application, such party shall be deemed to have no interest in further prosecution of its application, and its application may be dismissed with prejudice for failure to prosecute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file exceptions in denial cases may result in dismissal with prejudice for lack of prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Particularity and citation requirement for exceptions; waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: The consolidated supporting brief and exceptions shall point out with particularity alleged material errors in the decision or ruling and shall contain specific references to the page or pages of the transcript of hearing, exhibit or order on which the exception is based. Any objection not saved by exception filed pursuant to this section is waived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions must be specific and cite transcript/exhibit pages; failure to preserve objections by exception results in waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief in support of initial decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the period allowed for filing exceptions, any party may file a brief in support of an initial decision, in whole or in part, similar in form to the brief in support of exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits affirmative briefs supporting an initial decision to be filed within the same timeframe as exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page limits for consolidated brief/exceptions and replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Except by special permission, the consolidated brief and exceptions will not be accepted if the exceptions and argument exceed 25 double-spaced typewritten pages. The table of contents and table of citations are not counted. Within 10 days (or other time specified) any other party may file a reply brief, which shall not exceed 25 double-spaced pages and shall contain a table of contents and table of citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict page limits apply to exceptions/briefs and reply briefs; special permission required to exceed limits; attachments counted except tables of contents/citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting and granting oral argument on exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: If exceptions have been filed, any party may request oral argument not later than five days after the time for filing replies to the exceptions has expired. The Commission or delegated authority will grant oral argument by order only in cases where such oral presentations will assist resolution of the issues presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines for requesting oral argument; Commission's grant is discretionary and tied to usefulness for issue resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of intention to participate in oral argument; waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: Within five days after release of an order designating an initial decision for oral argument, any party who wishes to participate shall file a written notice of intention to appear and participate. Failure to file a written notice shall constitute a waiver of the opportunity to participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing timely written notice is required to preserve the opportunity to participate in oral argument; otherwise participation is waived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral argument scheduling and time allotment; extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each order scheduling a case for oral argument will contain the allotment of time for each party. The Commission will grant, in its discretion, upon good cause shown, an extension of such time upon petition by a party, which petition must be filed within 5 days after issuance of said order for oral argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time for argument is allocated in the scheduling order; extensions require a timely petition and showing of good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcripts — motions to correct and officer corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 10 days after a transcript of oral argument has been filed, any participant may file a motion requesting correction of the transcript, served on all other parties. Within 5 days after such motion, other parties may file pleadings in support or opposition. The officer who presided shall, by order, specify corrections to be made; the officer may on his own initiative specify corrections on 5 days notice to participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timelines for motions to correct transcripts and opportunity for responses; presiding officer issues orders specifying corrections and may act sua sponte with notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation by commissioners not present at oral argument
rubrics_metrics.description: Any commissioner who is not present at oral argument and who is otherwise authorized to participate in a final decision may participate in making that decision after reading the transcript of oral argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows absent commissioners to participate post-argument by reviewing the transcript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation of review to excepted issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon review of any initial decision, the Commission may, in its discretion, limit the issues to be reviewed to those findings and conclusions to which exceptions have been filed, or to those findings and conclusions specified in the Commission's order of review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission discretion to narrow review scope to excepted or specified findings/conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on exceptions to written-record rulings
rubrics_metrics.description: No party may file an exception to the presiding officer's ruling that all or part of the hearing be conducted and resolved on a written record, unless that party previously filed an interlocutory motion to request an oral hearing in accordance with §1.376.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must have previously sought an oral hearing (interlocutory motion) to later except to a ruling converting the hearing to a written record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required in Commission final decision
rubrics_metrics.description: After opportunity for filings and oral argument, the Commission will issue a final decision which shall contain: (1) findings of fact and conclusions, and the reasons or basis therefor, on all material issues presented on the record; (2) rulings on each relevant and material exception filed (irrelevant or non-decisional exceptions may be denied without the specific statement of reasons prescribed by paragraph (b)(1)); and (3) the appropriate rule or order and the sanction, relief or denial thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final decisions must explain factual and legal bases, rule on exceptions, and state the resulting order/sanction/relief; irrelevant exceptions may be dismissed without detailed reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of interlocutory matters (Commission vs presiding officer)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission acts on petitions to amend/modify/enlarge/delete issues in hearing proceedings which involve rulemaking matters exclusively. All other interlocutory matters in hearing proceedings are acted on by the presiding officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes interlocutory matters reserved for Commission (rulemaking-related issue amendments) from those handled by the presiding officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interlocutory pleading caption requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each interlocutory pleading shall identify the presiding officer in its caption. Unless the pleading is to be acted upon by the Commission, the presiding officer shall be identified by name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interlocutory pleadings must show who the presiding officer is; name required unless for Commission action.

rubrics_metrics.name: No reconsideration petitions for interlocutory rulings
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions requesting reconsideration of an interlocutory ruling will not be entertained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reconsideration petitions are not available for interlocutory rulings; other procedures (appeal/request) must be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interlocutory matters delay initial decision effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: No initial decision shall become effective under §1.276(e) until all interlocutory matters pending before the Commission in the proceeding at the time the initial decision is issued have been disposed of and the time allowed for appeal from interlocutory rulings of the presiding officer has expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures outstanding interlocutory matters/appeal windows are resolved before an initial decision becomes effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oppositions and replies to interlocutory requests — timing and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party may file an opposition to an interlocutory request. Except as provided or ordered otherwise, oppositions shall be filed within 4 days after the original pleading is filed, and replies to oppositions will not be entertained. Additional pleadings may be filed only if specifically requested or authorized by the person(s) who is to make the ruling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short timelines govern oppositions to interlocutory requests; replies normally not allowed; additional pleadings need authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of service requirement for certain pleadings
rubrics_metrics.description: No pleading filed pursuant to §1.51 or §1.294 will be considered unless it is accompanied by proof of service upon the parties to the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pleadings under these sections must be accompanied by proof of service or they will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral argument on contested interlocutory matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Oral argument with respect to any contested interlocutory matter will be held when, in the opinion of the person(s) who is to make the ruling, the ends of justice will be best served thereby. Timely notice will be given of the date, time, and place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presiding officer discretion to hold oral argument for interlocutory matters when justice requires; must provide timely notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing rules for ruling consideration and ex parte exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless irreparable injury/public interest/all parties consent otherwise, consideration of interlocutory requests will be withheld until the time for filing oppositions (and replies, if allowed) has expired. However, requests for continuances/extensions, permission to file pleadings in excess of chapter-prescribed length, and requests for temporary relief may be ruled upon ex parte without waiting for responsive pleadings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General rule is to wait for oppositions, but specific types of requests may be ruled on ex parte in the presiding officer's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral rulings and reasons for interlocutory rulings
rubrics_metrics.description: In the discretion of the presiding officer, rulings on interlocutory matters may be made orally to the parties. The presiding officer may state reasons on the record if transcribed, or may promptly issue a written statement of the reasons, either separately or as part of an initial decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulings may be oral; reasons may be given on the record or in writing promptly thereafter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interlocutory rulings appealable as of right — enumerated classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Rulings appealable as a matter of right include: (1) rulings denying or terminating a person's right to participate as a party; (2) rulings requiring testimony or production of documents over a privilege objection; (3) rulings denying a motion to disqualify the presiding officer or case manager; (4) rulings removing counsel from the hearing (appealable by counsel or client).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These specific interlocutory rulings may be appealed as of right and may not be deferred to exception to the initial decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission-to-appeal procedure for other interlocutory rulings
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for rulings appealable as of right, appeals shall be filed only if allowed by the presiding officer. A request for permission to appeal must be filed within 5 days after the order is released or the ruling is made. The request must show that the appeal presents a new/novel question of law or policy and that error would likely require remand if deferred; if a case manager made the ruling, show the question the case manager lacks authority to resolve. The presiding officer determines whether to allow the appeal. The Commission may dismiss an allowed appeal on the ground objection should be deferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets tight timing and required showing for obtaining interlocutory appeal permission; presiding officer screens requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures and page limits for appeals under §1.301 (5-page appeals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals filed under paragraph (a) or (b) shall be filed within 5 days (timing varies by subparagraph). The appeal shall conform to §1.49 and be subscribed/verified as in §1.52, served on parties, filed with Secretary, and shall not exceed 5 double-spaced typewritten pages. Oppositions shall be filed within 5 days after the appeal is filed. Replies are not permitted unless specifically requested. Oppositions and replies shall not exceed 5 double-spaced pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict formatting, verification, service, filing location, and short (5-page) page limits apply to these interlocutory appeals and responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal from final ruling by presiding officer (non-Commission) — timing and page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: If the presiding officer's ruling terminates a hearing, any party may appeal within 30 days after release. To preserve the right to appeal, file a notice of appeal within 10 days. If notice not filed within 10 days, ruling becomes effective 30 days after release and may be reviewed by Commission on its own motion within that period; absent an appeal following notice, ruling becomes effective 50 days after release. An appeal shall conform with §1.49 and §1.52, be served and filed with the Secretary, and shall not exceed 25 double-spaced typewritten pages. Oppositions to an appeal are filed within 15 days; replies to oppositions within 10 days and limited to matters raised; oppositions shall not exceed 25 pages; replies 10 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different timing and larger page limits apply to appeals from final rulings terminating proceedings (25-page limit), with explicit preservation steps and automatic-effect timeframes if notice is not timely filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery applicability and purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections 1.311 through 1.325 provide for depositions, interrogatories to parties, orders for production of documents and things, and for entry upon real property. These procedures may be used for discovery of relevant facts, for production and preservation of evidence for use in a hearing proceeding, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discovery tools are available for adjudications designated for hearing and for preserving evidence for use at hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of discovery procedures (adjudication/hearing)
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of discovery, these procedures may be used in any case of adjudication (as defined in the APA) which has been designated for hearing. For preservation of evidence, they may be used in any case designated for hearing and conducted under this subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discovery rules apply only to adjudications designated for hearing as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of examination for discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons and parties may be examined regarding any matter, not privileged, which is relevant to the hearing issues, including existence, description, nature, custody, condition and location of books, documents or things and identity/location of persons having knowledge of relevant facts. It is not ground for objection that the testimony will be inadmissible if it appears reasonably calculated to lead to discovery of admissible evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad relevance standard for discovery; non-privileged matters reasonably calculated to lead to admissible evidence are discoverable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on discovery from Commission personnel and records
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of discovery procedures against the Commission is subject to special limitations: informer's privilege covers info that may lead to an informer's identity; Commission personnel may not be questioned by deposition for discovery except on special order, but may be questioned by written interrogatories under §1.323 served on the appropriate Bureau Chief and answered/signed by personnel with knowledge; Commission records are not subject to discovery under §1.325 and inspection of records is governed by the FOIA and §§0.451–0.467.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discovery against the Commission is narrowly limited — interrogatories via Bureau Chief are allowed; depositions of Commission personnel require special order; records governed by FOIA rather than discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery schedule and presiding officer conference authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided by special order, discovery may be initiated after the initial conference (see §1.248(b)). The presiding officer may at any time order the parties/attorneys to appear at a conference to consider proper use of these procedures, the time to be allowed, and/or to hear argument and rule on disputes under the rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presiding officer controls discovery timing and may convene conferences to manage discovery scope and schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipulations regarding taking depositions
rubrics_metrics.description: If all parties so stipulate in writing and if there is no interference to the conduct of the proceeding, depositions may be taken before any person, at any time or place, upon any notice and in any manner; when so taken they may be used like other depositions. A copy of the stipulation shall be filed using ECFS and served on the presiding officer at least 3 days before the scheduled taking of the deposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties can agree to flexible deposition arrangements, but must file and serve the stipulation (ECFS + presiding officer) at least 3 days in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protective orders — scope and available measures
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer may issue any order consistent with these sections appropriate and just for protecting parties and deponents or providing for proper conduct. Rulings may specify measures including: that depositions not be taken or interrogatories not answered; that certain matters not be inquired into; that scope be limited to certain matters; that depositions be taken only at designated time/place or before a specified officer; that depositions be taken only by written interrogatories or only oral examination; that, after being sealed, the deposition shall be opened only by order of the presiding officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad protective-order authority to limit scope, method, timing, sealing, and use of discovery to prevent annoyance, expense, embarrassment, or oppression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation, filing, and service requirements for confidential materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Any information produced may be designated confidential pursuant to §§0.457, 0.459, or 0.461. Parties claiming confidentiality must: clearly mark each confidential page and narrowly tailor designation; file a public version redacting confidential info and mark it 'Public Version' (machine-readable when possible); remove confidential or privileged metadata from Public Version if necessary; file an unredacted 'Confidential Version' the same day, with header 'Confidential Version'; serve one copy of each version on attorney of record for each party and on the presiding officer, with proof of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed steps for creating and filing redacted public and confidential unredacted versions and serving them; confidentiality designation burden rests on designating party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited disclosure and use of confidential materials
rubrics_metrics.description: An attorney of record or party receiving unredacted confidential materials may disclose them only to: employees of counsel of record; officers/employees of receiving party directly involved in prosecution/defense; consultants or expert witnesses retained by the parties; and court reporters/stenographers — solely for use in prosecuting or defending the case and only to the extent necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure is strictly limited to a defined set of recipients and purpose-limited to the litigation; recipients must sign declarations acknowledging rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declarations, copy logs, and destruction/return of confidential materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Each individual authorized to receive confidential materials must sign a declaration/affidavit stating they reviewed the Commission's rules and understand limitations. Parties may make copies of confidential materials solely for use by the Commission or designated persons and must maintain a log recording number of copies and persons who received them. Upon final termination of the proceeding all originals and reproductions and the log shall be provided to the producing party, and notes or work product derived from confidential materials of an opposing or third party shall be destroyed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records and accountability obligations for confidential material access; return/destruction obligations at case termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirements for oral-deposition depositions (21-day notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: A party desiring to take a deposition upon oral examination shall give a minimum of 21 days' notice to every other party, the person to be examined, and the presiding officer or case manager, and file a copy of the notice with the Secretary/ECFS. The notice must include the name/address of each person (or sufficient description), the time/place and officer before whom deposition is to be taken, and the matters upon which each person will be examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum 21-day advance notice and required content for deposition notices; ECFS filing requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsive pleadings to deposition notices — timing and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 7 days after service of the notice to take depositions a motion opposing the taking may be filed by any party or the person to be examined. Within 14 days after service, a response to the opposition may be filed. Additional pleadings should not be filed; computation of time §1.4(g) does not apply to these pleadings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short, specified windows for filing motions opposing depositions and responses; generally no further pleadings allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to take depositions after opposition window
rubrics_metrics.description: If an opposition motion is not filed within 7 days and the presiding officer does not on his own motion issue a protective order prior to the date specified, the depositions described in the notice may be taken (no order required). If an opposition is filed, depositions shall not be taken until the presiding officer has acted. If a protective order is issued, depositions may be taken only in accordance with that order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default authorization to proceed with depositions after 7 days absent opposition or protective order; otherwise presiding officer's action is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may take depositions and compulsion of attendance
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositions shall be taken before specified officers (judges, clerks, notaries, etc.) or presiding officers as provided in §1.243. Attendance of witnesses at depositions may be compelled by subpoena as provided in §§1.331–1.340.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists authorized officers before whom depositions may be taken and confirms subpoena power to compel witness attendance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath, transcript, and electronic deposition methods
rubrics_metrics.description: The officer shall administer an oath/affirmation and shall record testimony stenographically or, upon approval by the presiding officer, by telephonic or electronically recorded methods including videotape. If these latter methods are used, parties may agree to waive provisions of paragraphs (e) and (f) as approved by the presiding officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic or telephonic deposition methods require presiding officer approval and may lead to agreed waivers of certain transcription/signing provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination methods and written-interrogatory option
rubrics_metrics.description: In oral-examination depositions, parties may proceed with examination and cross-examination as permitted at the hearing. In lieu of participating in the oral examination, parties served with the notice may transmit written interrogatories to the designated officer, who shall propound them to the witness and record the answers verbatim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may rely on written interrogatories administered by the officer in place of live participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission to witness, changes, signing, and certification of depositions
rubrics_metrics.description: When fully transcribed, the deposition shall be submitted to the witness for examination and read to/by him unless waived. Any changes in form or substance the witness desires to make shall be entered with reasons. The deposition shall then be signed by the witness unless signing is waived or witness unavailable or refuses; if unsigned, the officer shall sign and state the reason. The officer shall certify the deposition, seal it, and promptly send the original and two copies and exhibits with the notice/interrogatories by certified mail to the Secretary of the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures for witness review, correction, signing, certification, sealing, and filing of deposition originals and copies with the Commission Secretary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objections to depositions — pre-taking and at-taking rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Objections to the substance of any interrogatory or to examination on any matter clearly covered by the notice shall be made in a motion opposing the taking of depositions (prior to the taking) and not at the deposition. Errors and irregularities occurring at oral examination (manner of taking, form of questions/answers, oath, conduct, etc.) are waived unless reasonable objection is made at the taking. If objection is made, counsel shall attempt to agree on measures to obviate/cure errors; if no agreement, the objection shall be noted on the deposition and testimony taken subject to the objection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves rights by requiring timely objections (pre-deposition for substance; at-deposition for procedural irregularities) and encourages counsel to reach immediate accommodations; unresolved objections are noted and preserved on the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional at-taking objections and procedure for disputed lines of questioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Objections at the taking may be made on relevancy or privilege if notice did not clearly indicate the subject matter, or that the examination unreasonably annoys/embarrasses/oppresses a deponent. When there is objection to a line of questioning, counsel should attempt to agree on proper limits; if they cannot, depositions continue on non-objected matters and counsel shall within 24 hours either jointly or individually provide statements of their positions to the presiding officer (with telephone numbers) or otherwise jointly confer. The presiding officer shall promptly rule or take other appropriate action and give notice of the ruling to counsel and the officer taking the deposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes immediate procedures and 24-hour post-taking submissions to the presiding officer for resolving disputes about lines of questioning; presiding officer must act promptly and notify parties.
